evidence: src/application/errors/ErrorClassifier.ts: classifyError maps ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError to ErrorCategory. This is the only place that defines this mapping.

src/application/shared/requireFound.ts: requireFound<T> throws NotFoundError(entity, id) when a lookup returns undefined. It is the single guard used by AddTaskService, AssignTaskService, CompleteTaskService and ListTasksService.
src/application/ports/IdGenerator.ts: interface IdGenerator { next(): string } is an outbound port injected by the Create/Add services and implemented by UuidIdGenerator.
Both error-related files reuse the domain error types from src/domain/errors/DomainError.ts instead of redefining them, so no invariant is duplicated.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three unit files are the application layer's shared support for its use-case services. ErrorClassifier.ts turns domain errors into application-level categories. IdGenerator.ts defines the outbound port that the use-case services inject. requireFound.ts is a lookup guard that the task services share. The files sit in different subfolders (errors, ports, shared), but they all serve one concern: application-level plumbing around use cases. Each rule lives in one place. The 'missing entity becomes NotFoundError' rule exists only in requireFound, and the 'error type to category' mapping exists only in classifyError. Both rely on the domain's error hierarchy and don't redefine it, so nothing is duplicated. IdGenerator is a pure port with no logic. No file goes around a module abstraction. requireFound throws the domain NotFoundError, which is the same type that classifyError maps to 'not-found', so the two files are consistent with each other. The unit is small and somewhat mixed, but that is normal for a layer's shared helpers and does not meet the rubric's bar for unrelated concerns.
